topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: When I saw the space where my tree once stood, a flood of memories swept over me—sunlit afternoons of climbing, autumn leaves crunching underfoot, and the warmth of summer picnics in its shade. It’s a bittersweet reminder, but in every place the tree stood, there’s a story that’s grown, a bit of my childhood that’s rooted deep. I find myself smiling, thinking about all the saplings being planted today, each one a new chapter waiting to be written. There’s something wonderfully hopeful about that, about the cycle continuing, isn’t there? Maybe it’s time for a new tree, a new story.
